description: Team Red Harra is a Saudi-based team working with four AI agents to build Analog Arabia, an interactive atlas identifying and ranking underexplored Saudi volcanic fields, lava tubes, craters, and dune seas as potential Moon and Mars analog sites. Using NASA POWER, GIBS, and Moon/Mars Trek data, we connect Saudi Arabia’s unique geology with the future of planetary exploration.
summary: Analog Arabia is an interactive atlas that identifies and characterizes new, under-studied Moon and Mars analog sites in Saudi Arabia: volcanic fields, a 1.5 km lava tube, impact craters, an ancient lake, dune seas and Wadi Bisha. Users pick a mission (rover test, habitat trial, astrobiology, orbital instrument) and the tool ranks 10 Saudi sites against famous analogs (Atacama, Devon Island, Hawaii). Each site is paired with a NASA Moon or Mars target and uses live NASA POWER, GIBS and Moon/Mars Trek data. Well-characterized analogs help mission teams test equipment before flight, and this opens a new region for that testing.
details:
How it works: a weighted multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) scores each site 0-5 on 10 criteria. Two are measured live from NASA POWER (Mars-like climate from rainfall and sunlight; thermal cycling from daily temperature range), and eight are rated from cited scientific sources. Each mission is a set of weights.

Engineering: a month-by-month solar power engine sizes the panel array a habitat needs at each site, and two Monte Carlo tests (2,000 runs each) check whether the ranking holds.

Benefits: a sourced, ranked shortlist of new test sites, honest about its limits.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript on GitHub Pages; no server or keys.
